Definition: from G5235; a throwing beyond others, i.e. (figuratively) supereminence; adverbially (with G1519 or G2596) pre- eminently:--abundance, (far more) exceeding, excellency, more excellent, beyond (out of) measure.
BiblicalUsage: The word hyperbolḗ carries the sense of excess, abundance, surpassing excellence. In Romans 7:13, the text says "that sin by the commandment might become exceeding sinful." In 1 Corinthians 12:31, the text says "and yet shew I unto you a more excellent way."
TheologicalSignificance: For me, hyperbolḗ is a reminder that glory is the weight of who God is, and it is the end of everything He does. That shapes how I read the passages where it appears: not as filler, but as God's own wording for what He is doing.
